qt: to the Commission Hilde Vautmans (Renew) Subject:

Since 1 July 2026, a 0 % customs duty has been applied to sodium hydroxide originating in the United States, compared with the previously applicable rate of 5.5 %. This rate had already been in force for decades as the European Union’s common customs tariff. Sodium hydroxide is a key raw material for the European chemical industry. Furthermore, its production is energy-intensive, and European producers are already facing considerable pressure from international competition. 1.
What has the Commission’s assessment been of the impact of the reduction in the customs duty from 5.5 % to 0 % on the competitive position of European producers?

What were the specific reasons for including sodium hydroxide in the tariff elimination scheme, given that the 5.5 % tariff had been in place for many years and European producers are already facing considerable pressure from international competition, and has the Commission looked into any alternatives?
How will the Commission monitor the impact of this tariff elimination on European producers?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.11.2026) On 27 July 2025, the President of the Commission and the President of the United States reached a political agreement on tariffs and trade, later confirmed by the Joint Statement1 issued on 21 August 2025. As part of the political agreement, the EU committed to eliminate remaining custom duties on all industrial products (see paragraph one of the Joint Statement), including for sodium hydroxide. The tariff relief was implemented via Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 on the adjustment of customs duties on the import of certain goods originating in the United States of America and opening of tariff quotas for imports of certain goods originating in the United States of America2 and are in place since 1 July 2026. Article 7 of the Regulation foresees that the Commission will carry out a regular monitoring of the effects of the tariff elimination. Starting January 2027, the Commission will inform the European Parliament and the Council of the changes on quarterly basis about the changes in import values and volumes of goods within the scope of the Regulation. At present, there are insufficient data to make conclusions about the impacts of the Regulation on imports of sodium hydroxide. However, given that the volume of sodium hydroxide imports from the US has been increasing since 2024 but with little to no effect on the volume of intra-EU trade, the tariff free imports of sodium hydroxide from the US is not expected to impact the EU production considerably.
